13: # Feature Specification: Phase 1: template-drift-census-and-baseline
14: 
15: <!-- SPECKIT_LEVEL: 3 -->
16: 
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
21: 
22: This phase changes no system-spec-kit file. It produces two things every later phase depends on: a ledger with one row per defect, each row carrying the exact replacement text and a command that reproduces the defect, and a baseline of how a DeepSeek V4.1 Flash worker authors a Level 2 packet today. Phases 2 to 6 fix ledger rows. Phase 8 reruns the baseline and reports the change.
23: 
24: **Key Decisions**: three read-only census lanes split by directory, and three baseline runs of one fixed authoring task.
25: 
26: **Critical Dependencies**: the launch preconditions in `../spec.md` section 3: a build worktree, provider login and the three-lane authorization.
27: 
28: ---

30: ## 1. METADATA
31: 
32: | Field | Value |
33: |-------|-------|
34: | **Level** | 3 |
35: | **Priority** | P0 |
36: | **Status** | Draft |
37: | **Created** | 2026-10-23 |
38: | **Branch** | `main` |
39: | **Parent Spec** | ../spec.md |
40: | **Phase** | 1 of 8 |
41: | **Predecessor** | None |
42: | **Successor** | 002-template-and-example-defect-repair |
43: | **Handoff Criteria** | `scratch/ledger/ledger.jsonl` exists, every row reproduces, and `scratch/baseline/baseline.md` holds three runs |
44: <!-- /ANCHOR:metadata -->
45: 
46: ---
47: 
48: <!-- ANCHOR:phase-context -->
49: ## Phase Context
50: 
51: This is **Phase 1** of the Make system-spec-kit templates and authoring docs followable by a DeepSeek V4.1 Flash agent swarm specification.
52: 
53: **Scope Boundary**: Read-only on `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/`. Writes land only inside this phase folder, plus a throwaway track `specs/zz-bench-authoring/` that each baseline run creates and the conductor deletes.
54: 
55: **Dependencies**:
56: - The launch preconditions in `../spec.md` section 3 are met and recorded in `../goal.md` section 4.
57: 
58: **Deliverables**:
59: - `scratch/ledger/ledger.jsonl`: the merged, verified defect ledger.
60: - `scratch/baseline/hints-v2.2.txt`: every placeholder hint string a fresh Level 2 scaffold contains.
61: - `scratch/baseline/baseline.md` and `scratch/baseline/baseline.json`: three baseline runs with five metrics each.
62: 
63: **Changelog**:
64: - When this phase closes, refresh the matching file in ../changelog/ using the parent packet number plus this phase folder name.
65: <!-- /ANCHOR:phase-context -->
66: 
67: ---
68: 
69: <!-- ANCHOR:problem -->
70: ## 2. PROBLEM & PURPOSE
71: 
72: ### Problem Statement
73: Five template and doc defects are confirmed, but they came from a spot check, not a census, so the full list is unknown. Without a full list the repair phases would fix what someone happened to notice. Without a before-number, phase 8 cannot say whether the work helped a weak model at all.
74: 
75: ### Purpose
76: Every later phase works from one verified ledger, and phase 8 compares against measured numbers instead of an impression.
77: <!-- /ANCHOR:problem -->
78: 
79: ---
80: 
81: <!-- ANCHOR:scope -->
82: ## 3. SCOPE
83: 
84: ### In Scope
85: - Three read-only census lanes over the system-spec-kit templates, examples, template references, workflow references and `SKILL.md` router.
86: - A merged ledger in the frozen schema of `plan.md` section 3, with every row re-run by the conductor.
87: - The five confirmed defects present as ledger rows.
88: - Three baseline runs of the fixed authoring task in `tasks.md` T008.
89: - One read-only frontier review of the ledger before the phase closes.
90: 
91: ### Out of Scope
92: - Fixing any defect. Phases 2 to 6 own the fixes, and the `owner_phase` field routes each row.
93: - Editing any file under `.skilled/`. This phase is read-only there.
94: - Measuring models other than DeepSeek V4.1 Flash max. The question is about that model.
95: 
96: ### Files to Change
97: 
98: | File Path | Change Type | Description |
99: |-----------|-------------|-------------|
100: | `scratch/ledger/lane-a.jsonl`, `lane-b.jsonl`, `lane-c.jsonl` | Create | One file per census lane |
101: | `scratch/ledger/ledger.jsonl` | Create | Merged rows that reproduced |
102: | `scratch/baseline/hints-v2.2.txt` | Create | Hint strings from a fresh scaffold |
103: | `scratch/baseline/baseline.json`, `baseline.md` | Create | Three runs, five metrics |
104: | `scratch/briefs/*.txt` | Create | Every brief this phase dispatched |
105: | `tasks.md`, `goal.md`, `implementation-summary.md`, `acceptance-criteria.md` | Modify | Progress and evidence |
106: <!-- /ANCHOR:scope -->
107: 
108: ---
109: 
110: <!-- ANCHOR:requirements -->
111: ## 4. REQUIREMENTS
112: 
113: ### P0 - Blockers (MUST complete)
114: 
115: | ID | Requirement |
116: |----|-------------|
117: | REQ-001 | `scratch/ledger/ledger.jsonl` exists, every line parses as JSON, and every line has the ten fields of the frozen schema in `plan.md` section 3. |
118: | REQ-002 | For every ledger row, running its `evidence_cmd` prints its `evidence_expect` on the unchanged tree. |
119: | REQ-003 | The ledger holds a row for each of the five confirmed defects listed in `plan.md` section 3. |
120: | REQ-004 | `scratch/baseline/baseline.json` holds three runs, each with all five metrics. |
121: | REQ-005 | No file outside this phase folder differs from the phase start commit when the phase closes. |
122: 
123: ### P1 - Required (complete OR user-approved deferral)
124: 
125: | ID | Requirement |
126: |----|-------------|
127: | REQ-006 | A frontier review of the ledger ran, and each finding it raised is either applied to the ledger or recorded in `goal.md` section 4 with the reason it was not. |
128: 
129: > Acceptance criteria for these requirements live in `acceptance-criteria.md`,
130: > which is the document that decides whether this packet may close.
131: <!-- /ANCHOR:requirements -->
132: 
133: ---
134: 
135: <!-- ANCHOR:success-criteria -->
136: ## 5. SUCCESS CRITERIA
137: 
138: - **SC-001**: A conductor in phase 2 can turn any ledger row into a worker brief without asking anyone a question.
139: - **SC-002**: Phase 8 can compute a delta for each of the five baseline metrics.
140: <!-- /ANCHOR:success-criteria -->
141: 
142: ---
143: 
144: <!-- ANCHOR:risks -->
145: ## 6. RISKS & DEPENDENCIES
146: 
147: | Type | Item | Impact | Mitigation |
148: |------|------|--------|------------|
149: | Dependency | LLM Gateway provider for `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` | No lane or baseline run can start | The conductor runs the provider pre-flight in `plan.md` before the first dispatch and stops with a recorded blocker when it fails |
150: | Dependency | Build worktree can run `validate.sh` | Baseline metric M1 cannot be measured | `tasks.md` T002 proves it on an existing packet first |
151: | Risk | A lane worker invents a defect | False rows reach phase 2 | The conductor keeps only rows whose evidence command reproduces, and the frontier review reads the rest |
152: | Risk | A baseline run writes outside its throwaway track | The tree is dirty for phase 2 | Metric M4 counts those writes, and the conductor restores from the start commit before the next run |
153: <!-- /ANCHOR:risks -->
154: 
155: ---
156: 
157: 
158: ## 7. NON-FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS
159: 
160: ### Performance
161: - **NFR-P01**: Each census lane is one worker dispatch. A lane that has not returned in 30 minutes is killed by its captured PID and dispatched once more.
162: 
163: ### Security
164: - **NFR-S01**: Briefs carry no credential, token or key. Workers inherit provider login from the environment only.
165: 
166: ### Reliability
167: - **NFR-R01**: Every metric is computed by a command in `tasks.md`, so a second conductor running the same commands on the same runs gets the same numbers.
168: 
169: ---
170: 
171: ## 8. EDGE CASES
172: 
173: ### Data Boundaries
174: - Empty input: a lane that finds no defect writes an empty JSONL file, and the conductor records "0 rows" for it rather than re-dispatching.
175: - Maximum length: a row whose `expected_text` would exceed 2,000 characters is split into one row per paragraph.
176: 
177: ### Error Scenarios
178: - External service failure: a provider error such as a billing or region refusal stops the dispatch. The conductor records it and retries once after 10 minutes, then stops the phase.
179: - Network timeout: handled as in NFR-P01.
180: 
181: ---
182: 
183: ## 9. COMPLEXITY ASSESSMENT
184: 
185: | Dimension | Score | Triggers |
186: |-----------|-------|----------|
187: | Scope | 12/25 | Files: about 70 read, 0 changed outside this folder. Systems: templates, references, router |
188: | Risk | 6/25 | Auth: N, API: N, Breaking: N |
189: | Research | 14/20 | Full census of three directories plus a model baseline |
190: | Multi-Agent | 12/15 | Workstreams: 3 census lanes, 3 baseline runs, 1 review |
191: | Coordination | 8/15 | Dependencies: launch preconditions only |
192: | **Total** | **52/100** | **Level 3** |
193: 
194: ---
195: 
196: ## 10. RISK MATRIX
197: 
198: | Risk ID | Description | Impact | Likelihood | Mitigation |
199: |---------|-------------|--------|------------|------------|
200: | R-001 | Lane worker reports a defect that is not there | M | H | Reproduce-or-drop rule in `tasks.md` T006 |
201: | R-002 | Lane worker misses a defect class | M | M | Each lane brief lists the detection command for every class, and the frontier review reads the files again |
202: | R-003 | Baseline runs vary so much that a delta is noise | M | M | Three runs per side, and phase 8 reports the range, not only the mean |
203: 
204: ---
205: 
206: ## 11. USER STORIES
207: 
208: ### US-001: One row is one brief (Priority: P0)
209: 
210: **As a** phase 2 conductor, **I want** every defect as a row with its exact current text and its exact replacement, **so that** I can dispatch it as one worker brief with no judgment of my own.
211: 
212: **Acceptance criteria:** see `acceptance-criteria.md` (rows referencing this story).
213: 
214: ---
215: 
216: ### US-002: A before-number (Priority: P0)
217: 
218: **As the** operator, **I want** the authoring quality of DeepSeek V4.1 Flash measured before any template changes, **so that** the phase 8 result shows what the work changed.
219: 
220: **Acceptance criteria:** see `acceptance-criteria.md` (rows referencing this story).
221: 
222: ---
223: 
224: <!-- ANCHOR:questions -->
225: ## 12. OPEN QUESTIONS
226: 
227: - None that block this phase. Every choice it needs is frozen in `goal.md` section 1.
228: - A ledger row that a later phase cannot fix inside its frozen scope is recorded in that phase's goal log and raised to the operator, not absorbed.
229: <!-- /ANCHOR:questions -->
230: 
231: ---
232: 
233: ## RELATED DOCUMENTS
234: 
235: - **Implementation Plan**: See `plan.md`
236: - **Task Breakdown**: See `tasks.md`
237: - **Verification Checklist**: See `tasks.md`
238: - **Decision Records**: See `plan.md` section L3: ARCHITECTURE DECISION RECORD
239: 
240: ---

293: ## AI EXECUTION PROTOCOL
294: 
295: Written for the executing swarm. Follow each rule as written. Where a rule and your own judgment disagree, follow the rule and record the disagreement in `goal.md` section 4.
296: 
297: ### Roles
298: - **Conductor**: one DeepSeek V4.1 Flash max session that is not itself running inside OpenCode, because `cli-opencode` refuses a dispatch from inside OpenCode. It dispatches workers, runs every verify command, edits only this phase folder, and keeps `goal.md` section 4 current.
299: - **Worker**: one `opencode2 run` dispatch on `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max`. One worker does one lane or one baseline run, then stops.
300: - **Reviewer**: one read-only frontier review through `cli-codex` at phase close. It writes nothing.
301: 
302: ### Pre-Task Checklist
303: - [ ] Read this phase's `spec.md`, this plan and `tasks.md` before the first dispatch
304: - [ ] Read `.skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration/cli-opencode/SKILL.md` sections 3 and 4 before composing the first worker command
305: - [ ] Confirm the working directory is the build worktree recorded in `../goal.md` section 4, never the main checkout
306: - [ ] Confirm `opencode2 models --standalone` lists `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017`
307: - [ ] Save every brief to `scratch/briefs/<task-id>.txt` before dispatching it
308: 
309: ### Execution Rules
310: 
311: | Rule | Requirement |
312: |------|-------------|
313: | TASK-SEQ | Run tasks in ID order. Tasks marked `[P]` may run together, at most three at once, and only when no two write the same file |
314: | TASK-SCOPE | A worker writes only the paths under ALLOWED WRITE PATHS in its brief |
315: | TASK-VERIFY | The conductor runs the task's verify command and reads both its output and its exit status before marking the task `[x]` |
316: | TASK-LOCATE | Find text by its exact content, never by a line number |
317: | TASK-BANNED | Workers never run `git commit`, `git push`, `git checkout`, `git switch`, `git branch`, `git reset`, `git stash`, `generate-context.js` or `/speckit:save` |
318: 
319: ### Worker Brief Skeleton
320: 
321: Every brief starts with this block, word for word, with the two paths filled in:
322: 
323: ```text
324: GATE 3 IS PRE-RESOLVED. DO NOT ASK THE DOCUMENTATION-SCOPE QUESTION.
325: 
326: You are a non-interactive dispatched worker. AI_SESSION_CHILD=1 and
327: SYSTEM_SPEC_GATE_ENFORCE=0 are set in your environment, which this repository's AGENTS.md
328: defines as the autonomous child-dispatch exemption: the spec-folder question is pre-resolved
329: and MUST NOT be asked. No answer can reach you, because nobody is at a prompt.
330: 
331: Your write authority is already bound. The spec folder is:
332:   specs/system-speckit/054-weak-model-spec-authoring/001-template-drift-census-and-baseline
333: 
334: Proceed directly to the work. Do not print A/B/C/D options. Do not stop to confirm anything.
335: A failed edit match means a stale anchor: re-read the file and retry; halt only after three
336: failures on the same file.
337: Your task is complete only when files exist on disk and the verification command has been run.
338: 
339: ROLE: You are a read-only auditor. You read files, run read-only commands and write one
340: result file. Your output is checked line by line by a script.
341: 
342: ALLOWED WRITE PATHS:
343:   <the one file this task names>
344: 
345: BANNED OPERATIONS: git commit, git push, git checkout, git switch, git branch, git reset,
346: git stash, rm, mv, create.sh outside the task's stated command, generate-context.js,
347: /speckit:save, and any edit to a file not listed under ALLOWED WRITE PATHS.
348: ```
349: 
350: The role line is a focused persona summary in place of a full agent file, the small-context exception that `cli-opencode` rule 18 allows. It is declared here as that exception.
351: 
352: ### Dispatch Command
353: 
354: ```bash
355: cd "$WORKTREE" && SYSTEM_SPEC_GATE_ENFORCE=0 AI_SESSION_CHILD=1 opencode2 run --standalone \
356:   -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max --format json \
357:   "$(cat "$PHASE/scratch/briefs/$TASK.txt")" </dev/null > "$PHASE/scratch/runs/$TASK.jsonl" 2>&1 &
358: PID=$!; wait "$PID"; kill -9 "$PID" 2>/dev/null; pkill -9 -P "$PID" 2>/dev/null
359: ```
360: 
361: `PHASE` is this folder's path and `WORKTREE` is the build worktree. Never kill by a name pattern. Kill only the captured PID.
362: 
363: ### Status Reporting Format
364: 
365: `[T###] DONE | BLOCKED - one line of evidence`, written as a row in the progress table of `goal.md` section 4.
366: 
367: ### Blocked Task Protocol
368: 1. Restore any file the task changed with `git restore --source=<start commit> -- <file>`.
369: 2. Mark the task `[B]` in `tasks.md` with the failing command and the first line of its output.
370: 3. Re-dispatch at most twice with the brief corrected for what failed. After the third failure on the same task, leave it `[B]` and continue with the next task.
371: 4. Stop the phase when two tasks are blocked, and write `STOP` with both task IDs in `goal.md` section 4.
372: <!-- /ANCHOR:ai-execution -->

376: ## L3: ARCHITECTURE DECISION RECORD
377: 
378: ### ADR-001: Keep only rows that reproduce
379: 
380: **Status**: Accepted
381: 
382: **Context**: A DeepSeek worker asked to find defects will also report things that are not defects.
383: 
384: **Decision**: A lane row enters `ledger.jsonl` only when the conductor runs its `evidence_cmd` on the unchanged tree and the output contains its `evidence_expect`. The `self-contradiction` class has no command, so those rows go to the frontier review instead.
385: 
386: **Consequences**:
387: - Phase 2 receives no row it cannot reproduce.
388: - A real defect the worker described badly is dropped. The frontier review reads the source files again to catch those.
389: 
390: **Alternatives Rejected**:
391: - Trusting lane output as written: it puts unconfirmed findings into a repair phase that edits shared templates.
392: 
393: ### ADR-002: One fixed authoring task, three runs, run in a throwaway track
394: 
395: **Status**: Accepted
396: 
397: **Context**: The baseline must be rerun unchanged in phase 8, and one run of a sampling model is one sample.
398: 
399: **Decision**: The task text in `tasks.md` T009 is frozen. It runs three times per side. Each run creates `specs/zz-bench-authoring/`, and the conductor deletes that directory after measuring.
400: 
401: **Consequences**:
402: - Phase 8 compares like with like and reports a range.
403: - Three runs cannot detect a small effect. Phase 8 reports the range, not a significance claim.
404: 
405: **Alternatives Rejected**:
406: - Measuring by a frontier model's judgment of quality: one model is one opinion, and the five metrics are commands.

267: 2. **Baseline runs** - 1 to 2 hours - CRITICAL
268: 3. **Review** - 30 minutes - CRITICAL
269: 
270: **Total Critical Path**: about 2 to 3 hours
271: 
272: **Parallel Opportunities**:
273: - Lanes A, B and C run together, three dispatches at once, because they read disjoint directories and write separate files.
274: - The census lanes and the baseline runs do not share files, but the baseline waits for the lanes so that no more than three workers run at once.
275: <!-- /ANCHOR:critical-path -->
276: 
277: ---
278: 
279: <!-- ANCHOR:milestones -->
280: ## L3: MILESTONES
281: 
282: | Milestone | Description | Success Criteria | Target |
283: |-----------|-------------|------------------|--------|
284: | M1 | Setup done | T001 to T003 marked `[x]` with evidence | Start of phase |
285: | M2 | Ledger reduced | `ledger.jsonl` exists, every row reproduces | Mid phase |
286: | M3 | Baseline recorded | `baseline.json` holds three runs | Mid phase |
287: | M4 | Phase closeable | Every acceptance criterion `Met` | End of phase |
288: <!-- /ANCHOR:milestones -->
289: 
290: ---
291: 
292: <!-- ANCHOR:ai-execution -->
293: ## AI EXECUTION PROTOCOL
294: 
295: Written for the executing swarm. Follow each rule as written. Where a rule and your own judgment disagree, follow the rule and record the disagreement in `goal.md` section 4.
296: 
297: ### Roles
298: - **Conductor**: one DeepSeek V4.1 Flash max session that is not itself running inside OpenCode, because `cli-opencode` refuses a dispatch from inside OpenCode. It dispatches workers, runs every verify command, edits only this phase folder, and keeps `goal.md` section 4 current.
299: - **Worker**: one `opencode2 run` dispatch on `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max`. One worker does one lane or one baseline run, then stops.
300: - **Reviewer**: one read-only frontier review through `cli-codex` at phase close. It writes nothing.
301: 
302: ### Pre-Task Checklist
303: - [ ] Read this phase's `spec.md`, this plan and `tasks.md` before the first dispatch
304: - [ ] Read `.skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration/cli-opencode/SKILL.md` sections 3 and 4 before composing the first worker command
305: - [ ] Confirm the working directory is the build worktree recorded in `../goal.md` section 4, never the main checkout
306: - [ ] Confirm `opencode2 models --standalone` lists `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017`
307: - [ ] Save every brief to `scratch/briefs/<task-id>.txt` before dispatching it
308: 
309: ### Execution Rules
310: 
311: | Rule | Requirement |
312: |------|-------------|
313: | TASK-SEQ | Run tasks in ID order. Tasks marked `[P]` may run together, at most three at once, and only when no two write the same file |
314: | TASK-SCOPE | A worker writes only the paths under ALLOWED WRITE PATHS in its brief |
315: | TASK-VERIFY | The conductor runs the task's verify command and reads both its output and its exit status before marking the task `[x]` |
316: | TASK-LOCATE | Find text by its exact content, never by a line number |
317: | TASK-BANNED | Workers never run `git commit`, `git push`, `git checkout`, `git switch`, `git branch`, `git reset`, `git stash`, `generate-context.js` or `/speckit:save` |
318: 
319: ### Worker Brief Skeleton
320: 
321: Every brief starts with this block, word for word, with the two paths filled in:
322: 
323: ```text
324: GATE 3 IS PRE-RESOLVED. DO NOT ASK THE DOCUMENTATION-SCOPE QUESTION.
325: 
326: You are a non-interactive dispatched worker. AI_SESSION_CHILD=1 and
327: SYSTEM_SPEC_GATE_ENFORCE=0 are set in your environment, which this repository's AGENTS.md
328: defines as the autonomous child-dispatch exemption: the spec-folder question is pre-resolved
329: and MUST NOT be asked. No answer can reach you, because nobody is at a prompt.
330: 
331: Your write authority is already bound. The spec folder is:
332:   specs/system-speckit/054-weak-model-spec-authoring/001-template-drift-census-and-baseline
333: 
334: Proceed directly to the work. Do not print A/B/C/D options. Do not stop to confirm anything.
335: A failed edit match means a stale anchor: re-read the file and retry; halt only after three
336: failures on the same file.
337: Your task is complete only when files exist on disk and the verification command has been run.
338: 
339: ROLE: You are a read-only auditor. You read files, run read-only commands and write one
340: result file. Your output is checked line by line by a script.
341: 
342: ALLOWED WRITE PATHS:
343:   <the one file this task names>
344: 
345: BANNED OPERATIONS: git commit, git push, git checkout, git switch, git branch, git reset,
346: git stash, rm, mv, create.sh outside the task's stated command, generate-context.js,
347: /speckit:save, and any edit to a file not listed under ALLOWED WRITE PATHS.
348: ```
349: 
350: The role line is a focused persona summary in place of a full agent file, the small-context exception that `cli-opencode` rule 18 allows. It is declared here as that exception.
351: 
352: ### Dispatch Command
353: 
354: ```bash
355: cd "$WORKTREE" && SYSTEM_SPEC_GATE_ENFORCE=0 AI_SESSION_CHILD=1 opencode2 run --standalone \
356:   -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max --format json \
357:   "$(cat "$PHASE/scratch/briefs/$TASK.txt")" </dev/null > "$PHASE/scratch/runs/$TASK.jsonl" 2>&1 &
358: PID=$!; wait "$PID"; kill -9 "$PID" 2>/dev/null; pkill -9 -P "$PID" 2>/dev/null
359: ```
360: 
361: `PHASE` is this folder's path and `WORKTREE` is the build worktree. Never kill by a name pattern. Kill only the captured PID.
362: 
363: ### Status Reporting Format
364: 
365: `[T###] DONE | BLOCKED - one line of evidence`, written as a row in the progress table of `goal.md` section 4.
366: 
367: ### Blocked Task Protocol
368: 1. Restore any file the task changed with `git restore --source=<start commit> -- <file>`.
369: 2. Mark the task `[B]` in `tasks.md` with the failing command and the first line of its output.
370: 3. Re-dispatch at most twice with the brief corrected for what failed. After the third failure on the same task, leave it `[B]` and continue with the next task.
371: 4. Stop the phase when two tasks are blocked, and write `STOP` with both task IDs in `goal.md` section 4.
372: <!-- /ANCHOR:ai-execution -->
373: 
374: ---
375: 
376: ## L3: ARCHITECTURE DECISION RECORD
377: 
378: ### ADR-001: Keep only rows that reproduce
379: 
380: **Status**: Accepted
381: 
382: **Context**: A DeepSeek worker asked to find defects will also report things that are not defects.
383: 
384: **Decision**: A lane row enters `ledger.jsonl` only when the conductor runs its `evidence_cmd` on the unchanged tree and the output contains its `evidence_expect`. The `self-contradiction` class has no command, so those rows go to the frontier review instead.
385: 
386: **Consequences**:
387: - Phase 2 receives no row it cannot reproduce.
388: - A real defect the worker described badly is dropped. The frontier review reads the source files again to catch those.
389: 
390: **Alternatives Rejected**:
391: - Trusting lane output as written: it puts unconfirmed findings into a repair phase that edits shared templates.
392: 
393: ### ADR-002: One fixed authoring task, three runs, run in a throwaway track
394: 
395: **Status**: Accepted
396: 
397: **Context**: The baseline must be rerun unchanged in phase 8, and one run of a sampling model is one sample.
398: 
399: **Decision**: The task text in `tasks.md` T009 is frozen. It runs three times per side. Each run creates `specs/zz-bench-authoring/`, and the conductor deletes that directory after measuring.
400: 
401: **Consequences**:
402: - Phase 8 compares like with like and reports a range.
403: - Three runs cannot detect a small effect. Phase 8 reports the range, not a significance claim.
404: 
405: **Alternatives Rejected**:
406: - Measuring by a frontier model's judgment of quality: one model is one opinion, and the five metrics are commands.
407: 
408: ---

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# COMPONENT: CHECK PLACEHOLDERS
# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Scan spec folder .md files for remaining bracket placeholder
# Patterns after upgrade-level.sh + auto-populate.
# Bash 3.2+ compatible (macOS and Linux).
#
# This is the broad post-edit scan the quality hook runs: any bracket that
# still looks like a template placeholder. The validator rule at
# rules/check-placeholders.sh is narrower on purpose, flagging only the two
# canonical markers, so the two are not the same check with two homes.

set -euo pipefail

VERSION="1.0.0"

# Colors (disabled for non-TTY)
if [[ -t 1 ]]; then
    RED='\033[0;31m' GREEN='\033[0;32m' YELLOW='\033[1;33m' BOLD='\033[1m' NC='\033[0m'
else
    RED='' GREEN='' YELLOW='' BOLD='' NC=''
fi

# ─── Usage ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
usage() {
    cat <<EOF
Usage: $(basename "$0") <spec-folder> [OPTIONS]

Scan a spec folder for remaining bracket placeholder patterns.

Arguments:
  <spec-folder>    Path to spec folder (e.g., specs/042-feature/)

Options:
  --json           Output results in JSON format
  --verbose        Show each match with file and line number
  --help, -h       Show this help message

Exit codes:
  0  No placeholders found (PASS)
  1  Placeholders found (FAIL)
  2  Invalid arguments or folder not found

Examples:
  $(basename "$0") specs/042-feature/
  $(basename "$0") specs/042-feature/ --verbose
  $(basename "$0") specs/042-feature/ --json
EOF
}

# ─── Args ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
FOLDER_PATH=""
JSON_MODE=false
VERBOSE=false

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    case "$1" in
        --json)     JSON_MODE=true; shift ;;
        --verbose)  VERBOSE=true; shift ;;
        --help|-h)  usage; exit 0 ;;
        -*)         echo "Unknown option: $1" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2 ;;
        *)
            if [[ -z "$FOLDER_PATH" ]]; then
                FOLDER_PATH="$1"
            else
                echo "Error: unexpected argument '$1'" >&2
                usage >&2
                exit 2
            fi
            shift
            ;;
    esac
done

if [[ -z "$FOLDER_PATH" ]]; then
    echo "Error: spec folder path required" >&2
    usage >&2
    exit 2
fi

# Normalize trailing slash
FOLDER_PATH="${FOLDER_PATH%/}"

if [[ ! -d "$FOLDER_PATH" ]]; then
    echo "Error: folder not found: $FOLDER_PATH" >&2
    exit 2
fi

# ─── Placeholder patterns ────────────────────────────────────
# Match bracket patterns that look like template placeholders:
#   [Response time target], [Low/Med/High], [Component A],
#   [YOUR_VALUE_HERE], [PLACEHOLDER], etc.
#
# The templates write their stubs with the example inline, as in
# [Response time target - e.g., <200ms p95], [Uptime target - e.g., 99.9%]
# and [What problem we're solving], so the body admits < > + % and the
# apostrophe too. Without them those stubs pass the scan unfilled.
PLACEHOLDER_BODY="[A-Za-z0-9 /,._<>+%'-]"
#
# Exclude patterns that are NOT placeholders:
#   [x] / [ ] (checkbox), [P0] / [P1] / [P2] (priority tags),
#   [SPECKIT...] (markers), [ANCHOR...] (anchors),
#   [EVIDENCE...] (checklist evidence), [W:...] (workstream),
#   [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] (spec markers), [B] (blocked task)
#
# Also exclude lines where brackets appear inside code blocks
# (backtick-wrapped) since those describe placeholder concepts
# Rather than being actual unfilled placeholders.

TOTAL=0
MATCHES=""

# Process each .md file (skip backup/temp directories)
while IFS= read -r file; do
    # Skip backup directories and non-template subfolders.
    # Memory/ contains generated session context markdown that legitimately
    # Uses bracketed TOC links (e.g., [CONTINUE SESSION]); scratch/ is temp.
    case "$file" in
        */.backup-*) continue ;;
        */memory/*) continue ;;
        */scratch/*) continue ;;
        # research/ and review/ hold the deep loops' own output: iteration files,
        # dashboards and syntheses their workflow writes and regenerates, where
        # bracketed status text such as [None yet] is the reducer's format rather
        # than an unfilled template. The validator's placeholder rule reads only
        # the authored docs, so this scan matches it.
        */research/*) continue ;;
        */review/*) continue ;;
    esac

    line_num=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        line_num=$((line_num + 1))

        # Skip lines inside code fences or with backtick-wrapped brackets
        case "$line" in
            '```'*) continue ;;
            *'`['*) continue ;;
        esac

        # Skip HTML comments
        case "$line" in
            *'<!--'*'-->'*) continue ;;
        esac

        # Match bracket patterns that look like placeholders
        # Use grep to find [Something here] patterns
        if echo "$line" | grep -qE "\[[A-Z]${PLACEHOLDER_BODY}+\]" 2>/dev/null; then
            # Exclude known non-placeholder patterns
            cleaned="$line"
            # Remove known safe patterns before re-checking
            cleaned=$(echo "$cleaned" | sed -E \
                -e 's/\[x\]//g' \
                -e 's/\[ \]//g' \
                -e 's/\[P[0-2]\]//g' \
                -e 's/\[B\]//g' \
                -e 's/\[SPECKIT[^]]*\]//g' \
                -e 's/\[ANCHOR[^]]*\]//g' \
                -e 's/\[EVIDENCE[^]]*\]//g' \
                -e 's/\[NEEDS CLARIFICATION\]//g' \
                -e 's/\[W:[^]]*\]//g' \
                -e 's/`[^`]*`//g' \
                -e 's/\[[^]]*\]\(//g' \
            )

            # Check if any placeholder-like patterns remain after cleanup
            if echo "$cleaned" | grep -qE "\[[A-Z]${PLACEHOLDER_BODY}{2,}\]" 2>/dev/null; then
                TOTAL=$((TOTAL + 1))
                match_text=$(echo "$line" | grep -oE "\[[A-Z]${PLACEHOLDER_BODY}{2,}\]" 2>/dev/null | head -1)
                if [[ "$VERBOSE" == "true" ]]; then
                    MATCHES="${MATCHES}  ${file}:${line_num}: ${match_text}\n"
                fi
            fi
        fi
    done < "$file"
done < <(find "$FOLDER_PATH" -name "*.md" -type f 2>/dev/null | sort)

# ─── Output ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
if [[ "$JSON_MODE" == "true" ]]; then
    if [[ $TOTAL -eq 0 ]]; then
        echo "{\"status\":\"PASS\",\"placeholders\":0,\"folder\":\"$FOLDER_PATH\"}"
    else
        echo "{\"status\":\"FAIL\",\"placeholders\":$TOTAL,\"folder\":\"$FOLDER_PATH\"}"
    fi
else
    if [[ $TOTAL -eq 0 ]]; then
        echo -e "${GREEN}${BOLD}PASS${NC} — Zero placeholder patterns found in ${FOLDER_PATH}"
    else
        echo -e "${RED}${BOLD}FAIL${NC} — ${TOTAL} placeholder pattern(s) found in ${FOLDER_PATH}" >&2
        if [[ "$VERBOSE" == "true" && -n "$MATCHES" ]]; then
            echo ""
            echo -e "$MATCHES"
        fi
    fi
fi

# Exit code: 0 = pass, 1 = fail
if [[ $TOTAL -eq 0 ]]; then
    exit 0

3:description: "Codex CLI executor for OpenAI-backed coding, repo analysis, PR review, web research, and cross-model validation."
29:- **Web Research** — current internet info via the top-level `--search` flag (`codex --search exec …`), latest library versions, API changes, community solutions.
159:This packet owns user-facing routing, the `command -v codex` availability probe, prompt construction, and the self-invocation guard. Research and review lineages delegate process construction and execution to the already-shipped deep-loop runtime at `../../system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/fanout-run.cjs`, using executor kind `cli-codex`. That runner accepts only the `research` and `review` loop types, so a single build or doc dispatch uses the child dispatch envelope in [providers-and-models.md](./references/providers-and-models.md) §5.
161:The runtime is the single Codex execution adapter. Do not add a packet-local wrapper, command builder, or spawn path. Direct `codex exec` snippets below are operator reference and manual-testing examples; research and review lineages use the shared runtime, and a one-shot dispatch uses the child envelope.
177:| OAuth ready | 1 | Proceed with `codex exec --model gpt-5.5 -c model_reasoning_effort="medium" -c service_tier="fast"` |
192:**Default model + effort + tier**: `gpt-5.5` · `medium` reasoning · `fast` service tier. Balances speed, cost, and quality for the typical delegation.
197:codex exec \
198:  --model gpt-5.5 \
212:| (nothing specified) | `--model gpt-5.5 -c model_reasoning_effort="medium" -c service_tier="fast"` |
213:| "Use gpt 5.5 high fast" | `--model gpt-5.5 -c model_reasoning_effort="high" -c service_tier="fast"` |
214:| "Use gpt 5.5 low" | `--model gpt-5.5 -c model_reasoning_effort="low" -c service_tier="fast"` (fast stays unless user drops it) |
215:| "Use gpt 5.5 xhigh" | `--model gpt-5.5 -c model_reasoning_effort="xhigh" -c service_tier="fast"` |
216:| "Use gpt 6 luna max" | `--model gpt-6-luna -c model_reasoning_effort="max" -c service_tier="fast"` |
220:Honor whichever dimensions the user names. Model stays on `gpt-5.5` and service tier stays on `fast` unless the user explicitly names a different model or tier; keep the reasoning effort within the chosen model's ceiling (see Model Selection below and the roster in [references/providers-and-models.md](references/providers-and-models.md)).
224:`gpt-5.5` at `medium` on the `fast` service tier (`-c service_tier="fast"`) is the skill default for cross-AI delegation. Alternates: `gpt-6-luna` (≤ `max`), `gpt-5.6-terra` / `gpt-6-sol` (≤ `ultra`) — full roster, per-model effort ceilings, and the 8-level effort ladder in [references/providers-and-models.md](references/providers-and-models.md). Set effort with `-c model_reasoning_effort="<level>"` (there is **no `--reasoning-effort` flag**).
226:**Selection Strategy**: default `gpt-5.5 medium`; raise to `high` / `xhigh` for architecture, security, and complex planning; escalate the model when the task wants reasoning past `xhigh`; drop to `low` / `minimal` for trivial lookups. Per-task rationale table: [cli-reference.md](./references/cli-reference.md) §5.
241:Git diff review uses the built-in subcommand (no `-p`): `codex exec review "..." --commit HEAD`. Profiles may override `model`, `model_reasoning_effort`, `sandbox_mode`, `approval_policy`. The `.codex/agents/*.toml` files define personas for the interactive multi-agent TUI, NOT the `-p` flag.
247:- **`codex exec` defaults to `--sandbox read-only`** — file-modification tasks silently no-op (the agent plans changes but cannot write them). Pass `--sandbox workspace-write`; for headless no-prompt execution use top-level `-a never` before `exec` or `-c approval_policy=never`.
248:- **`--search` is a top-level flag, not an `exec` flag** — enable live web search as `codex --search exec …` (it precedes the subcommand). On codex ≥ 0.144 `codex exec --search` hard-fails with `unexpected argument '--search'` (older 0.125 builds accepted it), so treat any `exec … --search` example as stale. Without it, `codex exec` has no web access and answers from training data only — every dispatch needing live data (latest versions, repo facts, advisories) MUST use `codex --search exec …`.
249:- **Always pass `-c service_tier="fast"` explicitly** — this routes through the fast tier instead of whatever the caller's `~/.codex/config.toml` defaults to. Explicit means reproducible regardless of who runs it.
260:2. Delegate research and review lineages to `../../system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/fanout-run.cjs` with executor kind `cli-codex`. It rejects every other loop type, so a single build or doc dispatch uses the child dispatch envelope in [providers-and-models.md](./references/providers-and-models.md) §5. Never build a second adapter in this packet.
261:3. Use `--sandbox read-only` for review/analysis/research; `--sandbox workspace-write` for code generation/file modification — `codex exec` defaults to `read-only`, so omitting it causes silent no-op on edit tasks. For unattended approval, put top-level `-a never` before `exec` or set `-c approval_policy=never`.
264:6. **Redirect codex stdin from `/dev/null` on EVERY non-interactive dispatch** — not only inside a `while read` loop, which is the condition this rule used to name and the reason it was skipped. Pattern: `codex exec "$PROMPT" > "$LOG" 2>&1 </dev/null &`. Without `</dev/null`, the backgrounded codex process inherits the loop's stdin (the file after `done < input.jsonl`) and silently consumes the remaining lines — the loop exits after 3-6 iterations with no error. See `references/integration-patterns.md#background-execution` → "Silent Stdin Consumption".
265:7. **Specify model + effort + service tier explicitly** — never rely on caller environment. Default: `--model gpt-5.5 -c model_reasoning_effort="medium" -c service_tier="fast"`. Honor user overrides verbatim. Use `high`/`xhigh` for reasoning-heavy tasks (architecture, security, deep planning).
266:8. Route to the appropriate `-p <profile>` when the task matches a specialization (see Section 3 routing table); use `codex exec review` (built-in subcommand) for git diff reviews.
269:   1. **Fast path (default).** Build from the local `assets/prompt-quality-card.md`, which delegates the framework table + CLEAR check to the canonical card.
271:11. **Never inject user-level voice/personalization content into AI-orchestrated Codex delegations.** Codex CLI reads user-level voice from `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` (the human's global settings, loaded automatically). When an AI delegates via `codex exec`, the calling AI's own voice rules govern the response — do NOT read `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` and paste into delegation prompts. Keep delegations focused on task/model/sandbox/effort/(spec-folder pre-approval). If the user asks how to make Codex sound more like Claude in *their own* sessions, point to `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` — not any repo asset.
275:15. **Single-dispatch discipline (operator-gated, session-scoped)** — Default: launch ONE cli-* dispatch at a time across the cli-* family (cli-codex, cli-opencode, cli-claude-code). Wait for the dispatched agent's work to return, verify outputs exist, then SIGKILL only the dispatch THIS skill started: capture its PID at launch (`codex exec ... & CODEX_PID=$!`) and kill that captured PID directly plus its own orphan children (`kill -9 "$CODEX_PID" 2>/dev/null; pkill -9 -P "$CODEX_PID" 2>/dev/null`), then apply the same PID-scoped `gtimeout` cleanup. **Never use a blanket `pkill -9 -f "codex exec --model"` pattern** — that matches and kills EVERY running `codex exec` process on the machine, including the operator's unrelated codex sessions. Only launch the next dispatch (this skill OR a sibling) after the prior one is dead and RSS has dropped. **Within a deep-flow session** (deep-review / deep-research): the operator authorizes the whole multi-iteration session at start — iterations chain back-to-back with kill-between as the safety mechanism, NOT a per-iteration confirmation prompt. **Exception (cross-skill parallel)**: when the operator explicitly authorizes N parallel dispatches, run N concurrently — but still SIGKILL each by its own captured PID as its work returns.
276:16. **Set `AI_SESSION_CHILD=1` in the dispatched child's env AND state the exemption in the prompt.** The variable makes the waiver true; it does not make it observable. The reader being waived is a model, and a model cannot see an environment variable, so a child given only the variable still stops to ask the documentation-scope question and writes nothing, at exit code zero. Copy the preamble from [`shared/references/child-dispatch-preamble.md`](../shared/references/child-dispatch-preamble.md) to the top of every non-interactive prompt. when sessions may be launched through the per-session worktree wrapper (`.skilled/bin/worktree-session.sh`). A dispatched `codex exec` is an orchestrated sub-session, not a new top-level session, so it must SHARE the parent's worktree rather than allocate its own. The wrapper checks `AI_SESSION_CHILD` (plus a `git --git-common-dir` structural backstop) and exec's in place when set. Pattern: `AI_SESSION_CHILD=1 codex exec ... </dev/null`. Harmless when the wrapper is not in use. See `.skilled/bin/README.md` → "Worktree session isolation".
278:17. **Agent-persona injection (attach identity, not just the task).** Every dispatch composes `{resolved agent persona + task prompt}` — never a bare task. Resolve the persona from the ACTIVE runtime's agent directory per AGENTS.md §9 (`.skilled/agents/<name>.md`, `.claude/agents/<name>.md`, etc. — never hardcode one runtime), and map each subtask to the RIGHT agent (`code`→code, `review`→review, `design`→design, research→`deep-research`, docs→`markdown`), not one default. **Codex has no native persona surface** — `.codex/agents/*.toml` is TUI-only, and `codex exec` / `-p <profile>` load sandbox/effort config, not a persona. So **INLINE** the persona block into the prompt payload on every dispatch, using the same in-payload pattern as the `DESIGN_DISPATCH_MANIFEST` (Rule 14) — the child cannot resolve agent paths by reference. A persona-less dispatch runs the leaf as a generic assistant, silently dropping the agent's tool-scope, verification gates, and output contract. Canonical contract: `../../sk-prompt/assets/cli-prompt-quality-card.md` "Persona Injection"; native precedent: `orchestrate.md` "Agent Loading Protocol". Rare exceptions (focused summary for a small-context model, pure-mechanical command) are declared at the dispatch site.
280:18. **Never dispatch `codex exec` from inside a running codex session.** A codex process cannot spawn another codex from inside its own sandbox. The nested child dies at startup with `failed to initialize in-process app-server client: Operation not permitted` (observed 2026-09-02 on codex-cli 0.151.0 under `--sandbox workspace-write`), and the parent reads that as a failed iteration rather than a route violation. So when codex is itself the executor of a deep-loop fan-out lineage or any other orchestrating session, it must do each iteration's work in-process with its own tools and never dispatch a second codex. Grep that exact message to confirm you are hitting this and not a model or network fault.
288:5. Build or maintain a packet-local Codex execution adapter; the deep-loop runtime is the execution authority.
346:- Appropriate Codex profile and sandbox level matched to task type (read-only for review, workspace-write for generation).
347:- Orchestrated execution delegated to the shared deep-loop runtime without a packet-local adapter.

On codex ≥ 0.144 `codex exec --search` hard-fails with `unexpected argument '--search'` (older 0.125 builds accepted it), so treat any `exec … --search` example as stale. Without it, `codex exec` has no web access and answers from training data only — every dispatch needing live data (latest versions, repo facts, advisories) MUST use `codex --search exec …`.
249:- **Always pass `-c service_tier="fast"` explicitly** — this routes through the fast tier instead of whatever the caller's `~/.codex/config.toml` defaults to. Explicit means reproducible regardless of who runs it.
260:2. Delegate research and review lineages to `../../system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/fanout-run.cjs` with executor kind `cli-codex`. It rejects every other loop type, so a single build or doc dispatch uses the child dispatch envelope in [providers-and-models.md](./references/providers-and-models.md) §5. Never build a second adapter in this packet.
261:3. Use `--sandbox read-only` for review/analysis/research; `--sandbox workspace-write` for code generation/file modification — `codex exec` defaults to `read-only`, so omitting it causes silent no-op on edit tasks. For unattended approval, put top-level `-a never` before `exec` or set `-c approval_policy=never`.
264:6. **Redirect codex stdin from `/dev/null` on EVERY non-interactive dispatch** — not only inside a `while read` loop, which is the condition this rule used to name and the reason it was skipped. Pattern: `codex exec "$PROMPT" > "$LOG" 2>&1 </dev/null &`. Without `</dev/null`, the backgrounded codex process inherits the loop's stdin (the file after `done < input.jsonl`) and silently consumes the remaining lines — the loop exits after 3-6 iterations with no error. See `references/integration-patterns.md#background-execution` → "Silent Stdin Consumption".
265:7. **Specify model + effort + service tier explicitly** — never rely on caller environment. Default: `--model gpt-5.5 -c model_reasoning_effort="medium" -c service_tier="fast"`. Honor user overrides verbatim. Use `high`/`xhigh` for reasoning-heavy tasks (architecture, security, deep planning).
266:8. Route to the appropriate `-p <profile>` when the task matches a specialization (see Section 3 routing table); use `codex exec review` (built-in subcommand) for git diff reviews.
269:   1. **Fast path (default).** Build from the local `assets/prompt-quality-card.md`, which delegates the framework table + CLEAR check to the canonical card.
271:11. **Never inject user-level voice/personalization content into AI-orchestrated Codex delegations.** Codex CLI reads user-level voice from `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` (the human's global settings, loaded automatically). When an AI delegates via `codex exec`, the calling AI's own voice rules govern the response — do NOT read `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` and paste into delegation prompts. Keep delegations focused on task/model/sandbox/effort/(spec-folder pre-approval). If the user asks how to make Codex sound more like Claude in *their own* sessions, point to `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` — not any repo asset.
275:15. **Single-dispatch discipline (operator-gated, session-scoped)** — Default: launch ONE cli-* dispatch at a time across the cli-* family (cli-codex, cli-opencode, cli-claude-code). Wait for the dispatched agent's work to return, verify outputs exist, then SIGKILL only the dispatch THIS skill started: capture its PID at launch (`codex exec ... & CODEX_PID=$!`) and kill that captured PID directly plus its own orphan children (`kill -9 "$CODEX_PID" 2>/dev/null; pkill -9 -P "$CODEX_PID" 2>/dev/null`), then apply the same PID-scoped `gtimeout` cleanup. **Never use a blanket `pkill -9 -f "codex exec --model"` pattern** — that matches and kills EVERY running `codex exec` process on the machine, including the operator's unrelated codex sessions. Only launch the next dispatch (this skill OR a sibling) after the prior one is dead and RSS has dropped. **Within a deep-flow session** (deep-review / deep-research): the operator authorizes the whole multi-iteration session at start — iterations chain back-to-back with kill-between as the safety mechanism, NOT a per-iteration confirmation prompt. **Exception (cross-skill parallel)**: when the operator explicitly authorizes N parallel dispatches, run N concurrently — but still SIGKILL each by its own captured PID as its work returns.
276:16. **Set `AI_SESSION_CHILD=1` in the dispatched child's env AND state the exemption in the prompt.** The variable makes the waiver true; it does not make it observable. The reader being waived is a model, and a model cannot see an environment variable, so a child given only the variable still stops to ask the documentation-scope question and writes nothing, at exit code zero. Copy the preamble from [`shared/references/child-dispatch-preamble.md`](../shared/references/child-dispatch-preamble.md) to the top of every non-interactive prompt. when sessions may be launched through the per-session worktree wrapper (`.skilled/bin/worktree-session.sh`). A dispatched `codex exec` is an orchestrated sub-session, not a new top-level session, so it must SHARE the parent's worktree rather than allocate its own. The wrapper checks `AI_SESSION_CHILD` (plus a `git --git-common-dir` structural backstop) and exec's in place when set. Pattern: `AI_SESSION_CHILD=1 codex exec ... </dev/null`. Harmless when the wrapper is not in use. See `.skilled/bin/README.md` → "Worktree session isolation".
278:17. **Agent-persona injection (attach identity, not just the task).** Every dispatch composes `{resolved agent persona + task prompt}` — never a bare task. Resolve the persona from the ACTIVE runtime's agent directory per AGENTS.md §9 (`.skilled/agents/<name>.md`, `.claude/agents/<name>.md`, etc. — never hardcode one runtime), and map each subtask to the RIGHT agent (`code`→code, `review`→review, `design`→design, research→`deep-research`, docs→`markdown`), not one default. **Codex has no native persona surface** — `.codex/agents/*.toml` is TUI-only, and `codex exec` / `-p <profile>` load sandbox/effort config, not a persona. So **INLINE** the persona block into the prompt payload on every dispatch, using the same in-payload pattern as the `DESIGN_DISPATCH_MANIFEST` (Rule 14) — the child cannot resolve agent paths by reference. A persona-less dispatch runs the leaf as a generic assistant, silently dropping the agent's tool-scope, verification gates, and output contract. Canonical contract: `../../sk-prompt/assets/cli-prompt-quality-card.md` "Persona Injection"; native precedent: `orchestrate.md` "Agent Loading Protocol". Rare exceptions (focused summary for a small-context model, pure-mechanical command) are declared at the dispatch site.
280:18. **Never dispatch `codex exec` from inside a running codex session.** A codex process cannot spawn another codex from inside its own sandbox. The nested child dies at startup with `failed to initialize in-process app-server client: Operation not permitted` (observed 2026-09-02 on codex-cli 0.151.0 under `--sandbox workspace-write`), and the parent reads that as a failed iteration rather than a route violation. So when codex is itself the executor of a deep-loop fan-out lineage or any other orchestrating session, it must do each iteration's work in-process with its own tools and never dispatch a second codex. Grep that exact message to confirm you are hitting this and not a model or network fault.
288:5. Build or maintain a packet-local Codex execution adapter; the deep-loop runtime is the execution authority.
346:- Appropriate Codex profile and sandbox level matched to task type (read-only for review, workspace-write for generation).
347:- Orchestrated execution delegated to the shared deep-loop runtime without a packet-local adapter.

  ```bash
  for l in a b c; do
